messages:
incident-bot: PagerDuty alert fired for service=llm-batch-fanout, urgency=high, incident_id=PD-102983. Trigger: repeated 5xx bursts and duplicate fanout across regions. @Alyssa you are next on-call.

pagerbot: auto-claim by Alyssa (oncall). Incident assigned to: Alyssa (oncall). Escalation policy: oncall -> sme -> eng-sre. :rotating_light:

Alyssa (oncall): I see the spike. Checking dashboards, traces. First pass: looks like routerd is sending the same request to multiple consumers because batch window misaligned across replicas.

Samir: ack. I can jump on routerd. Any customer-facing impact?

Mira: customer reports show ~12k requests with 50-150ms extra latency and ~0.6% 5xx for last 3m. Affected endpoints: /v1/generate (hosted). Sending CUST-IMPACT note now.

Alyssa (oncall): Good, thanks Mira. @Taylor (sre) can you check if the batch coalescer has a misapplied config from yesterday rollout? I remember a change to the jitter window (was 10ms -> 50ms).

Taylor (sre): On it. Pulling routerd config.

ops-bot: deploy-hook: rollout of routerd/2026.03.14-jnk-8 completed in prod us-east-1 at 2026-03-14T21:12:03Z. Can be the cause if config was baked into image.

Samir: Found a diff in config: batch.window_ms = 50 for new release; old was 5. Also batch-coordinator still using edge clock sync that can vary by ~40ms across hosts. That combination can cause duplicate fanout shards.

Alyssa (oncall): That explains duplicate fanout — small jitter + larger window => overlapping windows. Mitigation plan: 1) reduce batch.window_ms to 10 on routerd config 2) enable strict dedupe on fanout path for 60s 3) temporarily scale down routerd from 6 replicas -> 3 in affected region to reduce overlap.

Mira: I can post a short customer status: "We saw transient duplicate request delivery causing increased errors for a small subset of requests. Engineers are mitigating; updates in 20m." :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Taylor (sre): Applying quick patch to configmap in prod-us-east-1, will push to canary first.

Samir: Before patching, capturing a short log sample. Logs: ```
[routerd] 2026-03-14T21:34:01Z INFO batch window start=1617 end=1667 host=routerd-2
[routerd] 2026-03-14T21:34:01Z WARN duplicate-send detected req_id=abc123 shard=7
[worker] 2026-03-14T21:34:01Z ERROR downstream 502 id=abc123
```

Alyssa (oncall): Nice capture. Taylor, can you push the canary then promote if green? Keep PD incident open until stable.

Taylor (sre): Canary patch applied to routerd-3 (canary). Observing for 2m.

pagerbot: PD note: Alyssa acknowledged, Samir assigned as secondary. PagerDuty incident PD-102983 updated.

Mira: Canary looks good so far. No duplicate-send warnings in the canary logs. 0.02% 5xx in canary window.

Samir: Preparing the rollback plan if promotion fails: revert image tag and reapply batch.window_ms=5 config.

Alyssa (oncall): If canary is stable at +5m, promote. Also enable temporary routing dedupe middleware flag (dedupe=true) for 10m across us-east-1. I'll coordinate with support for customer comms.

Taylor (sre): Promoting patch now to remaining routerd replicas in us-east-1. Executing: `kubectl -n prod set env deploy/routerd BATCH_WINDOW_MS=10` then `kubectl rollout restart deploy/routerd`.

ops-bot: kubectl: rollout started for deploy/routerd (prod us-east-1).

Samir: Post-promotion logs show duplicates dropping to near-zero. Example: ```[routerd] 2026-03-14T21:41:12Z INFO batch window start=2204 end=2214 host=routerd-5
```

Mira: Metrics: 5xx back to baseline 0.02% across region. Latency back to normal. Crafting update: "Mitigation deployed; customers should see restored service. We'll keep monitoring and follow up with root cause." :white_check_mark:

Alyssa (oncall): Great. Closing immediate customer impact. Leaving PD incident open for a short RCA follow-up. Can someone pick up an RCA doc? Samir?

Samir: I can own RCA. Will open doc and ping with timeline. Quick notes: root cause = interaction of increased batch.window_ms and unsynchronized host clocks leading to overlapping batch windows; secondary cause = lack of short-term dedupe on fanout path.

Alyssa (oncall): Thanks. Timeline: we started detecting at t=21:31, mitigation complete at t=21:42. I'll mark the incident as acknowledged/resolved once RCA is filed.

pagerbot: Incident PD-102983 status: acknowledged -> mitigated. Incident bridge cleared. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Post-incident checklist reminder: add config guardrail to prevent batch.window_ms > 20 without staged rollout, add automated dedupe toggle default=false but quick-enable route, add clock-sync check in preflight for routerd host pool.

Mira: Noted. I'll add customer postmortem notify to the post-incident doc and draft the support message.

Alyssa (oncall): Thanks team. Good catch and quick mitigation. Closing thread after RCA doc created. 

Samir: RCA doc created: https://redwood.atlassian.com/browse/RCA-102983 — will add timeline and follow-ups.

Taylor (sre): Leaving a follow-up ticket to add a unit test around batch window interaction.

ops-bot: Reminder: runplaybook: run incident postmortem template -> assigned Samir, due 2026-03-18.

Alyssa (oncall): Closing PD incident now in PagerDuty. Thanks everyone. :bow:
notes: This thread documents an automated PagerDuty page and the live mitigation/ownership coordination for a batch fanout timing race that caused duplicate sends and customer 5xxs. Key actors and mitigation steps included config rollback, canary promotion, and enabling a dedupe middleware. RCA owner assigned.
